# XER Schedule Check: DCMA 14-point assessment of a Primavera P6 XER file

> Free, in-browser DCMA 14-point schedule check for Primavera P6 .xer exports. It reads the XER tables, recomputes early and late dates and total float on each activity's own calendar with P6's relationship, lag-calendar, constraint and progress rules (equal to P6's stored values on 19,820 of 19,822 open activities, 99.99%, in six public files from P6 5.0 to 24.12; free float on 19,810), runs the 14 points with the DCMA thresholds and a 600-day critical path test, and lists every activity behind each finding, plus logic loops, out-of-sequence progress and open finishes. It also compares two monthly updates of one project: progress claimed, actual dates edited after reporting, logic, duration, constraint and calendar changes, float used, driving-path changes, and a half-step run that splits the finish movement into progress and revisions. A Monte Carlo risk run draws every open activity's remaining duration from a triangular range (a default the user replaces, or per-activity days) and gives P10/P50/P80/P90 finish dates, the chance of the forecast and must-finish dates, and each activity's criticality index and sensitivity; an optional risk register (events with a probability and a delay range on named activities) shows the contingency the events add at P80 and ranks each event by how far it moves the finish. Resource levelling delays not-started activities until every resource stays within its maximum units per hour from the file (by early start, then the file's levelling priority, then total float; successors carried by the same CPM engine) and gives the levelled finish, every activity moved and the resource that moved it, peak use before and after, a lower bound no levelling can beat, and a crew-size what-if. The assessment, comparison and risk run feed a written review an owner's rep can print to PDF and send: corrections ranked high, medium and low with the exact activities behind each, and, after a risk run, a finish date risk section (the ranges assumed, P10-P90 with and without the register, events ranked, the activities that drive the finish) with corrections for a must-finish date met in under 80% of runs, near-critical activities off the driving path that drive the finish in a quarter or more of runs, and a forecast met in under half the runs with no stated contingency. Nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Screening metrics on the user's own file, not scheduling, contractual or legal advice. Missed tasks and BEI use P6's planned dates as the baseline because a single XER rarely carries the baseline project. Not modelled: expected finish dates, multiple float paths; resource levelling is a serial pass like P6's (not P6's code), so its levelled dates can differ from P6's; the risk ranges are the user's assumption, not data in the file, and resource limits and probabilistic branches are not modelled. Not affiliated with Oracle, Primavera or the DCMA.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/xer-schedule-check/)

## For agents

- Engine: `xer.mjs` `parseXer(decodeXer(bytes))`; `cpm.mjs` `schedule(xer)` (dates in wall-clock minutes, float in hours) and `drivingPath(result, projId)`; `dcma.mjs` `assess(xer, { projId })` returns `{ project, checks[14], extra, recompute, activities, drivingPath }`, `findingsCsv(report)` and `scheduleCsv(report)` (every open activity's recomputed dates, total and free float beside the stored values).
- `compare.mjs` `compare(prevXer, curXer)` returns `{ previous, current, finish: { moved, halfStep, progressEffect, revisionEffect }, flags, progress, logic, durations, constraints, calendars, activities, float, criticalPath }`; `compareCsv(rep)`, `compareText(rep)`.
- `report.mjs` `reviewItems(assessment, comparison?, risk?)` returns the ranked corrections `[{ severity, source, action, measure, items }]`; `riskItems(risk)` the risk-based ones alone (thresholds in `RISK_LIMITS`); `reviewHtml(assessment, comparison?, { recipient, reviewer, reference, notes, date, limit, risk })` returns a self-contained, script-free HTML review to print or save as a PDF.
- `risk.mjs` `riskAnalysis(xer, { projId, iterations, range: { min, likely, max }, correlation, ranges, risks, seed })` returns `{ project, percentiles[{ p, date, days, overDeterministic }], pDeterministic, pMustFinish, histogram, activities[{ code, name, criticality, sensitivity, deterministicCritical }], risks[{ id, probability, targets, occurred, finishShift, shiftNoise, notNoise }], withoutRisks{ percentiles, pDeterministic, eventDelay }, warnings }`; `parseRisks(csvText)` reads `id,probability,min,likely,max,activity...` (probability as 0.3 or 30%, days); `parseRanges(csvText)` reads `code,min,likely,max` in working days; `riskAnalysisAsync` runs in slices for a page; `riskCsv(result)`.
- CLI: `node cli.mjs schedule.xer --risk [N] [--range 90,100,125] [--correlation 0.3] [--ranges ranges.csv] [--risks register.csv] [--seed S] [--csv drivers.csv] [--json] [--report review.html]` (with `--report` the review carries the risk section; also with `--previous`); `node cli.mjs schedule.xer [--report review.html [--to NAME] [--from NAME] [--ref TEXT] [--notes TEXT]] [--json] [--csv out.csv] [--schedule activities.csv] [--project CODE]`; `node cli.mjs current.xer --previous previous.xer [--json] [--csv changes.csv] [--project CODE]` (the previous file's project is matched by project ID; CSV cells that would run as spreadsheet formulas are written as text).

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/xer-schedule-check): MIT licensed. Measurements: `eval/cpm-vs-p6-2026-11-19.md`, `eval/free-float-2026-11-19.md` (free float equals P6's on 19,810 of 19,822 activities), `eval/compare-check-2026-11-19.md`, `eval/review-report-2026-11-19.md` (the written review on the six public files), `eval/risk-check-2026-11-19.md` (the risk run on the same six files), `eval/risk-register-check-2026-11-19.md` (risk register events: planted events against the CPM engine), `eval/review-risk-check-2026-11-19.md` (the risk section and its corrections in the written review on the six files).
